the_signal.headline: AI audit trails and governance shift from nice-to-have to compliance requirement
the_signal.body: n8n's new audit trail framework for production workflows signals that enterprises now demand execution records and data usage tracking as table stakes, not differentiators. For GTM engineers selling into regulated verticals (finance, healthcare, SaaS), this is the compliance moat you've been missing—build it now or lose deals to competitors who have.

tool_drop.name: n8n AI Agent Governance Framework
tool_drop.what: Enterprise-grade agent inventory, least-privilege access control, and runtime guardrails built directly into workflow orchestration.
tool_drop.why: Eliminates the 'but how do we audit this?' objection that's currently blocking agent adoption in Fortune 500 deals.

thread_of_day.title: The Orchestration Chasm: Why AI Maturity Isn't Linear
thread_of_day.takeaway: Organizations don't progress smoothly through AI maturity levels—there's a specific transition point (the orchestration chasm) where most stall between proof-of-concept and production scale.

quote.text: There is a specific transition point where organizations do not advance evenly through maturity levels.
quote.source: n8n Blog — AI Maturity: Bridging the Orchestration Chasm

whats_moving.context: Three separate n8n posts on governance, audit trails, and incident response signal that the market has moved past 'can we build an agent' to 'can we govern it safely.'
n8n's expanded compliance automation content suggests enterprise buyers are consolidating their regulatory stack into workflow platforms rather than point solutions.
n8n's direct comparison of Claude Code positioning versus workflow orchestration indicates this boundary (code vs. config) is now a core GTM battleground.

act_on_this: Audit your current agent deployment for missing execution logs and data provenance tracking—if you can't answer 'who accessed what data and when,' you're one compliance question away from losing a six-figure deal.

numbers.stat: 75 capabilities expected in production agent development tools, but only partially solved across major platforms
numbers.context: This gap is why agent projects stall in production—you need a checklist to hold vendors accountable and avoid building missing pieces yourself.
